subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler GPU offering — follow-up & next tests
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Brian Chen <brian.chen@vectorai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + next tests: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler follow-up

Hi Brian — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of the discussion and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

1) Goals/priorities you called out:
- Capacity guarantees for peak traffic (esp. 9–11am PST spikes)
- Predictable unit economics (cost per 1k tokens at sustained throughput)
- Model parity for Llama-3-70B (or comparable family) and support for quantized variants
- VPC/private deployment and compliance evidence for procurement

2) How Redwood typically approaches this evaluation (high level):
- Dedicated reserved pool for predictable throughput (we surface guaranteed vCPU/GPU pool + soft burst)
- Smart routing to fall back to hosted variants if reserved pool is saturated
- Prefix/KV caching and request batching to reduce per-token cost while keeping latency SLOs

3) Proposed tests / PoC plan (what we recommend to compare against hyperscaler reserved instances):
- Throughput test: sustained 1k QPS (50–512 token responses depending on prompt), 2 clients for 30m windows
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 250ms for <512 tokens, p99 < 600ms target (happy to adjust)
- Failure modes: simulate GPU OOM and verify automated fallback to warm standby model variant
- Cost sampling: run identical request stream against hyperscaler reserved instances and Redwood Dedicated to compare $/1k tokens and end-to-end cost (including networking and infra overhead)

I attached a short one-pager that highlights the differentiated controls we discussed (reserved pool semantics, SLA, routing policies, observability hooks). Attachment: 20260520-redwood-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler.pdf

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to provide benchmark config + API keys for the PoC (I’ve CC’d her)
- Schedule technical deep-dive (60m) next week to align on test harness and sequences (suggest Wed/Thu)
- High-level procurement ask: if PoC looks good, start committed-reserved discussion (term + capacity)

Would Wed 5/27 10am PT work for a technical deep-dive?

Best,
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Brian Chen <brian.chen@vectorai.com>

Subject: Re: Quick recap + next tests: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler follow-up

Thanks Markus — that summary is super helpful. A few clarifying points from our side before we lock in the technical deep-dive:

- Primary priority is absolute capacity guarantees during peak windows. Our ops team will not accept *best-effort* burst on the hyperscaler — they want committed capacity with defined failover behavior.
- VPC/private deployment requirement: we need to ensure there’s no cross-tenant leakage and that egress/integration into our data plane is straightforward.
- Model: we are primarily evaluating Llama-3-70B (fp16 and q4 variants). Can Redwood serve the same weights and support quantized runs?
- Cost: please prepare an initial apples-to-apples pricing sketch (committed capacity case vs equivalent reserved EC2/GPU + managed infra).

Procurement will want the SOC2 + data handling summary and a short runbook for incident escalation. I’ll loop them in after the technical deep-dive.

Wed 5/27 10am PT works for a 60m deep-dive for me — confirm and I’ll send a calendar hold.

Onwards,
Brian
Head of ML Ops, VectorAI

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-05-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next tests: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler follow-up

Appreciate the clarity Brian. Short answers and next actions below:

- Committed capacity: yes — Redwood Dedicated supports reserved GPU pools with explicit capacity guarantees (we can commit X GPUs for a term and expose guaranteed throughput; see the one-pager). If desired we can include an SLA clause for minimum effective throughput and an automatic fallback policy that routes to a compatible hosted variant when the pool is exhausted.
- VPC/private deployment: supported. We offer a private control plane and customer-managed networking (VPC peering / private link) — Laura, I’ll need your standard network checklist for their infra team.
- Model compatibility: we support Llama-3 family and can serve both fp16 and qX variants. For large-model inference we recommend quantized runs for cost efficiency; we’ll include an apples-to-apples perf run for fp16 vs q4x to show tradeoffs.
- Pricing sketch: I’ll put together a simple committed vs hyperscaler reserved comparison for the PoC (Rishi — FYI, please draft the initial numbers and margin assumptions).

Proposed PoC timeline:
- May 27: technical deep-dive (agree Wed 10am PT)
- Jun 1–28: 4-week PoC (throughput + failover tests)
- By week 5: results review + procurement pricing conversation

Action items:
- Laura: benchmark config + test harness and API keys
- Rishi: preliminary committed pricing sketch for the PoC
- Brian: calendar hold for 5/27 10am PT

Thanks — looping internal team to get the configs ready.

Best,
Markus

Subject: PoC benchmark config & checklist

Markus / Brian — putting a proposed bench config here so we can lock it before the deep-dive. I pushed the same checklist to the shared PoC doc (link in related_links).

Benchmark config (initial):
- Model: Llama-3-70B (fp16) and Llama-3-70B (q4x) runs
- Instance/reserved pool: start with equivalent of 2 x A100-80GB reserved for Redwood Dedicated (we can right-size after baseline run)
- Client load: 2 load clients, 1k QPS sustained target, each request ~64 tokens input / 128 tokens generation median (we will sample longer tails)
- KV cache: enabled for repeated prefixes (we’ll enable prefix caching to measure effective token reduction)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, token/sec, error rate, and routing fallbacks (count)
- Failure simulation: intentionally OOM one worker after 20 minutes to validate fallback behavior

Checklist for pre-PoC network/security:
- VPC peering or PrivateLink details (CIDRs, egress rules)
- KMS/HSM keys for model encryption if required
- Required SOC2 / security docs (Markus, I attached the standard security packet in the shared folder)

I’ll prepare a shell script and a k6 load test harness that we can run; Markus, can you confirm we have the appropriate test tokens for VectorAI?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
